parts.label: a
parts.description: Using the series for e^x, write down the first four terms of the Maclaurin series for e^(-2x).
parts.notes: M1 for substituting -2x into the series for e^x. A1 for all four terms. Wrong method: leaving out the factorials (1 - 2x + 4x^2 - 8x^3): M1A0.

parts.label: b
parts.description: Hence find the Maclaurin series of f(x) = (1 + 3x)e^(-2x) up to x^3.
parts.tolerance: Exact coefficients required. Terms beyond x^3 may be shown or omitted.
parts.notes: M1 for multiplying their series by (1 + 3x). A1 for all products up to x^3. A1 for 1 + x - 4x^2 + (14/3)x^3. A derivative route (f(0), f'(0), f''(0), f'''(0)) earns full marks.

parts.label: c
parts.description: Hence write down f''(0).
parts.notes: A1 for -8 (2! times the x^2 coefficient). Wrong method: the coefficient -4 itself: A0. 'Write down': no working needed.
parts.follow_through: FT from (b): 2 times their x^2 coefficient.

parts.label: a
parts.description: Find the acceleration at t = 4.
parts.notes: M1 for a = dv/dt = 2t - 7. A1 for 1. Wrong method: v(4) = -2 is the velocity: M0A0.

parts.label: b
parts.description: Find the values of t for which the particle is at rest.
parts.tolerance: Both values required for the A1.
parts.notes: M1 for setting v = 0 and solving (factorizing, formula or GDC). A1 for both t = 2 and t = 5.

parts.label: c
parts.description: Find the total distance travelled for 0 <= t <= 6.
parts.tolerance: Accept 15. The GDC value of the modulus integral is acceptable with the integral shown.
parts.notes: M1 for the integral of |v| from 0 to 6, or for splitting at t = 2 and t = 5 and adding the sizes. A1 (implied) for the three pieces 26/3, 9/2 (or -9/2), 11/6. A1 for 15. Wrong methods: the displacement integral of v = 6: M0A0A0; splitting only at t = 2 (26/3 + 8/3 = 34/3): M1A0A0.
parts.follow_through: FT from the candidate's roots in (b).

source: Original (2026-10-28). f(x) = ln(1 + sin x): derivatives, Maclaurin series to x^3, limit, series integral on [0, 0.4] with percentage error.

parts.label: a
parts.description: Show that f'(x) = cos x/(1 + sin x) and f''(x) = -1/(1 + sin x).
parts.notes: A1 for f'(x) by the chain rule. M1 for the quotient (or product) rule applied to f'(x). A1 for using sin^2 x + cos^2 x = 1 to reach -(1 + sin x)/(1 + sin x)^2 or equivalent; restating the given result with no simplification shown earns A0.

parts.label: b
parts.description: Find f'''(x).
parts.tolerance: Accept any equivalent form, e.g. (1 + sin x)^-2 cos x.
parts.notes: M1 for differentiating -(1 + sin x)^-1 with the chain rule (or the quotient rule). A1 for cos x/(1 + sin x)^2.

parts.label: c
parts.description: Hence find the Maclaurin series for f(x) up to and including the x^3 term.
parts.notes: A1 for all four values f(0), f'(0), f''(0), f'''(0). M1 for the Maclaurin formula with their values. A1 for x - x^2/2 + x^3/6. Wrong method: dividing by n instead of n! gives x^3/3: A0.

parts.label: d
parts.description: Use part (c) to find the limit as x -> 0 of (ln(1 + sin x) - x)/x^2.
parts.notes: M1 for substituting the series and simplifying to -1/2 + x/6 (or equivalent). A1 for -1/2. The question says to use part (c): l'Hopital's rule with the correct answer earns M0A1.

parts.label: e
parts.description: Use part (c) to approximate the integral of ln(1 + sin x) from 0 to 0.4, and find the percentage error.
parts.tolerance: Accept any value consistent with the candidate's own series and correctly-rounded values. A value cut short without an ellipsis earns A0 (3 s.f., exact, or the display with an ellipsis).
parts.notes: M1 for integrating their series term by term on [0, 0.4]. A1 for 0.0704. A1 for the percentage error 0.209%, computed relative to the true (GDC) value. Wrong method: dividing by the approximation gives 0.208%: A0 for the percentage error.

parts.label: a
parts.description: By solving a differential equation, show that v = 30/(1 + 0.6t).
parts.notes: M1 for separating the variables: integral of v^-2 dv = integral of -0.02 dt. A1 for -1/v = -0.02t + C. M1 for using v = 30 at t = 0 to find C. A1 for a line leading to the given form, e.g. 1/v = (0.6t + 1)/30. Verifying the given answer by differentiation earns at most M0A0M0A0 (the question says 'by solving').

parts.label: b
parts.description: Find the time at which the speed is 12 m s^-1.
parts.notes: M1 for setting 30/(1 + 0.6t) = 12. A1 for 2.5.

parts.label: c
parts.description: Find the distance travelled in this time.
parts.tolerance: Accept 45.8, 50 ln 2.5, or the display with an ellipsis. The GDC value of the integral is acceptable with the integral shown. A value cut short without an ellipsis earns A0 (3 s.f., exact, or the display with an ellipsis).
parts.notes: M1 for the integral of v from 0 to their t. A1 (implied) for 50 ln(1 + 0.6t) or 50 ln 2.5. A1 for 45.8. Wrong method: constant deceleration (30 + 12)/2 x 2.5 = 52.5: M0A0A0.

parts.label: d
parts.description: Given a = v dv/ds, find v in terms of s.
parts.tolerance: Accept any equivalent form, e.g. ln v = -0.02s + ln 30 rearranged.
parts.notes: M1 for separating: integral of (1/v) dv = integral of -0.02 ds. A1 for ln v = -0.02s + C with C = ln 30 found from v = 30 at s = 0. A1 for v = 30e^(-0.02s).

parts.label: e
parts.description: Hence find the speed after travelling 100 m.
parts.tolerance: Accept 4.06 or 30e^-2. A value cut short without an ellipsis earns A0 (3 s.f., exact, or the display with an ellipsis).
parts.notes: M1 for substituting s = 100 into their v(s). A1 for 4.06. Wrong method: t = 100 in v(t) gives 0.492: M0A0.

parts.label: a
parts.description: Use the differential equation to find f'(0), f''(0), f'''(0).
parts.notes: A1 for f'(0) = 2. M1 for differentiating the equation implicitly (y'' = 1 + 2y'). A1 for f''(0) = 5. A1 for f'''(0) = 10. Wrong method: differentiating x as 0 (y'' = 2y', giving 4 and 8): M0A0A0.

parts.label: b
parts.description: Hence find the Maclaurin series for y up to x^3.
parts.notes: M1 for the Maclaurin formula with their values. A1 for the correct series. Dividing by n instead of n! shows only in the x^3 term (10/3): A0.

parts.label: c
parts.description: By using an integrating factor, solve the differential equation.
parts.notes: M1 for an integrating factor from y' - 2y = x. A1 for e^(-2x). M1 for integration by parts on x e^(-2x). A1 for -(x/2)e^(-2x) - (1/4)e^(-2x) + C. A1 for the final answer with C = 5/4 found. Wrong methods: integrating factor e^(2x): M1A0, later marks FT; a sign slip in the parts (giving (3/4)e^(2x) - x/2 + 1/4): A0 for the integral and the final A1.

parts.label: d
parts.description: Use the series to estimate f(0.2) and find the percentage error.
parts.tolerance: Accept any value consistent with the candidate's own series and exact solution, or with a GDC value of the true solution. A value cut short without an ellipsis earns A0 (3 s.f., exact, or the display with an ellipsis).
parts.notes: A1 for the estimate 1.51333... (3 s.f. or display). A1 for the percentage error 0.0956%, relative to the true value.
